play_name: Let things unfold before you manage them
behavioral_target: Trying to control the unknown by needing a plan for everything and bracing for disappointment early.
trigger: Something about the relationship feels open, unknown, or like it could go wrong.
old_play: You make a plan to feel in control, or you brace for the letdown before it comes.
function_of_old_play: Both moves ease the not-knowing right now and help you feel safer.
new_play: Name what feels unknown or what you fear. Then let one small thing stay open and watch what really happens instead of managing it ahead of time.
what_to_expect: The open feeling is uncomfortable, and you may be let down for real. But you get to see how things actually go.
why_supports_task: Sitting with some not-knowing lets you see the relationship as it really is, instead of steering or guarding it. This work does not sit in one relationship phase.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Preparing for disappointment before it happens
context_limitations: Plans and caution are useful at times. This is about when you need control over everything and can't leave room to see how things unfold on their own.
review_reason: Cross-Phase source gap: no competency maps and there is no single developmental task. STM-0952 is Insufficient Evidence, so it is contextual only, not behavioral evidence.
